textos.txt: Do you feel the cold, Maria? Here, even time seems to freeze...
But don't be deceived: a sample forgotten in the ice can lose its representativeness as quickly as an icicle melts under the sun
The real challenge here is not only preservation... it's traceability, recordkeeping, and ensuring every step is documented
So it's not enough to just store it in the cold?
You also need to know where it is, how long it stayed, and who handled it?
Exactly. A sample without traceability is like a snowflake lost in a blizzard
Prepare yourself. I will test if you truly understand how to keep under control what must be preserved
Which of the following alternatives represents a **nonconformity** with item 7.4 of ISO/IEC 17025, regarding traceability and control of stored samples?

alternativas.txt: The laboratory keeps records of entry, use, and disposal of each calibration item, ensuring full traceability.
Samples are labeled with codes, status, and expiration dates, visible throughout the storage period.
Samples that have not yet been used have no records at all, since they are considered “at rest.”
The storage system allows quick tracking of the location and condition of each stored sample.
Records related to sample handling are updated whenever there are relevant movements or status changes.

textos.txt: In the ice, everything seems still... but without traceability, even what is preserved can be lost
Control is the warmth that keeps trust in results alive
Move forward, Maria... harsher environments still await you
